title: Tenpura: A General Transient Fault Evaluation and Scope Narrowing Platform for Ultra-fast Reliability Analysis
problem: Simulation-based fault injection for reliability analysis is impractically slow (months to years for large designs); most transient faults are harmless, creating inefficiency.
motivation: Reliability analysis pre-deployment requires efficient fault evaluation for critical systems.
method: Tenpura uses FPGA emulation—running the chip design on reconfigurable hardware instead of pure software simulation—to speed up the testing process. It traces which parts of the hardware are actively used by reading scan chains (built-in test circuits that read internal state). Since faults occurring in inactive hardware can't affect the chip's operation, the system only injects faults into active regions. This scope narrowing dramatically reduces the fault-testing workload compared to testing every possible transient fault.
key_novelty: The key innovation is using scan-chain activity data to identify which transient faults could matter, enabling ultra-fast pre-silicon fault injection.
contributions: Transient fault scope narrowing via scan-based activity tracing
FPGA emulation acceleration for fault injection
One month analysis vs months-to-years for simulation-based FI

metrics.speedup: One month analysis vs months-to-years for SOTA
metrics.other: 88.49-96.26% fault reduction across RISC-V cores and NVDLA accelerator

limitations: Pre-silicon only; scope narrowing may miss critical faults; evaluation limited to three DUTs (RISC-V cores and NVDLA).
